
=================================================================
#24 Yeon’s Massacre  (642 October)
Arc: Iron Will · place: pyongyang · tone: coup horror
Logline: All summer he has bowed. Now he’s hosting a banquet, and the king is coming.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Everyone in Pyongyang agrees that a man who bows all summer has learned his place.
[1] ¶ Yeon's father dies in the spring, in his own bed in the east. The seal should pass to the son. The Summit takes the whole summer to admit it. When it finally does, Yeon decides to host a banquet. The king is in attendance.
[2] [MAP 642: ]
[3] ¶ All summer he has bowed. He went to every seat at the Summit one at a time and asked for his father’s seal like a younger son asking for an inheritance. Among themselves they have already agreed that he will have it for one winter, out on the border forts, and not come back.
[4] ── SCENE: The Banquet ──
[5] ¶ October cold sits under the eaves. The lamps are already lit when the Five Commanderies take their seats — wine first, then meat, then the old joke that Pyongyang never runs out of either. Each commander wears a ring-pommel sword at his hip, the three-legged crow stamped in the ring. The hall smells of sesame oil and autumn horse-sweat brought in on Eastern boots.
[6] King Youngryu: Ah — so even the renowned Gesomun has learned to bow… / Your father would have liked to see it.
[7] King Youngryu: Good — everyone is here. / We settle the succession today.
[8] King Youngryu: Gesomun! So you kneel at last!
[9] King Youngryu: Ah—
[10] Yeon Gesomun: I… will take responsibility for my own fate from now on…! / **May Your Majesty live ten thousand years….!**
[11] ¶ Every door in the hall closes at once, from the outside.
[12] ¶ The side doors were never for servants. When they open again, Yeon’s soldiers come through every one of them. Tables overturn. Wine becomes a darker color before anyone names it. Yeon does not shout orders. He walks the length of the room the way a man walks a border he has already decided to keep, and he takes each commander’s blade himself.
[13] ¶ First the Southern Commander. He wanted the next levy for Yushin’s passes, and called Eastern fighting easy work.
[14] Son Daeha: Yeon…! / Samhan… the Samhan His Majesty named—
[15] Yeon Gesomun: Son Daeha. / You asked for men, not speeches. / I am taking the men.
[16] ¶ He draws the Southern ring-pommel from a belt that no longer needs it. One crow. One weight on the spine to come.
[17] ¶ Then the Northern Commander. He would not freeze another winter while the capital counted his remounts twice.
[18] Go Ul: The horses… still in… the warehouses…
[19] Yeon Gesomun: Go Ul. / …The three villages. I remember them.
[20] ¶ The Northern crow joins the first. Outside, a horse screams in the yard and then does not.
[21] ¶ The Western Commander had warned that this would gift the Tang a road. He dies looking west, as if the road might still be argued shut.
[22] Go Heumsong: The Liao… / The Emperor’s drums…
[23] Yeon Gesomun: You were right about the road.
[24] ¶ Three crows. The hall’s lamps lean as if listening.
[25] ¶ **Lee Gaesa** carries no banner. He is the Summit’s clerk, and he wrote its verdict on Yeon: one winter on the border, and do not come back. Tonight he has wine in his mouth, and then nothing.
[26] Lee Gaesa: Traitor…! / That day… I…
[27] Yeon Gesomun: Lee Gaesa. / You wrote me one winter. / I am giving you one night.
[28] ¶ Four. The verdict becomes metal he can wear.
[29] ¶ Last of the banners: his uncle. The soft voice that told a nephew to sit down, because the Summit does not run on prophecies.
[30] Yeon Gusesa: Nephew… / Traitor… a feast… like this…
[31] Yeon Gesomun: Uncle. / You told me to sit down. / You called me traitor for standing. / …. / A Yeon takes this one from a Yeon.
[32] ¶ Five ring-pommels. Five crows. Yeon wipes none of them clean.
[33] ¶ He finally approaches **King Youngryu** for the final blow. The crown has slid. The Samhan dream is still in the king’s mouth, too late to be a budget.
[34] King Youngryu: Gesomun… / With gold… decades… / The King for All…
[35] Yeon Gesomun: Your Majesty. / The gold was never going to be enough. The Tang emperor had already priced your head. / **May You live ten thousand years.**
[36] ¶ Yeon places each of the **Five Blades** onto his own back.
[37] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun): He wore five swords on his body, and no one around him dared look up at him. Every time he mounted or dismounted, he made nobles and generals lie on the ground and stepped on them.❞
[38] ¶ He steps into the doorway with the blades on his back. Red-wing chalgap fills the door.
[39] Yeon Gesomun: Loyal men of Goguryeo — hear the words of Yeon Gesomun! / In the south, Baekje and Silla covet us, / and in the west the Second Emperor comes this way, butchering nation after nation! / And all the while an incompetent king and rotten ministers shut their eyes to the world and lead this country down the road to ruin!! / Silla and the East, then Baekje the next day, then the Tang!
[40] Yeon Gesomun: But what of the people? We have nowhere else to go! / We live on this land, we die on it, and we are the ones who bleed every time they come! / The world will call us mad! Of course — to take your own fate in your own hands has always looked like madness to the world!
[41] Yeon Gesomun: **No one is coming to save us!!** Only we can do it — with our own hands!!
[42] ¶ In the aftermath, Yeon enthrones the king’s nephew as **King Bojang** and creates a new position for himself, as the **Supreme Commander**.
[43] Yeon Gesomun: You there… what is your name?
[44] King Bojang: M-my name? My surname is Go—
[45] Yeon Gesomun: You there… what is your name?
[46] [CARD King Bojang: The old king’s nephew. He has been given a crown and very little to do with it.]
[47] [CARD Yeon Gesomun — Supreme Commander of Goguryeo: A chair he built himself, above every other chair in the room.]
[48] ¶ He makes one more appointment before the blood is dry. **Dosuryu** — an old friend of the Yeon house, one of the few men who has ever told him no and lived — is named **Grand Herald**, a post that did not exist until the banquet needed a voice that was not the throne’s.
[49] Dosuryu: Grand Herald… / I have had you by the scruff since your father was alive. / And now you want that mouth to read the country aloud?
[50] Yeon Gesomun: If you will not, who will. / That Bojang… I only need the name. / The one who speaks to the people is you.
[51] Dosuryu: Very well. / Only — for as long as you still listen to me. / If you stop, I am a herald, not a friend.
[52] ¶ Yeon listens. Not always. Often enough that the court learns which door to fear besides his.
[53] ── SCENE: The Temples ──
[54] ¶ After the blood dries, Yeon looks at the temples. They are rich, and they pray for whoever is winning. He has an idea about that, which can wait. One young monk named **Shinsung** learns how to wait too.
[55] Yeon Gesomun: Pray quieter. / Or pray to something that does not own half the capital.
[56] [CARD Shinsung: A monk of Pyongyang. Very quiet, and very well connected.]
[57] Shinsung: Amitabha.
[58] ❝QUOTE (Sutra of Forty-two Sections (四十二章經), attr. Kāśyapa Mātaṅga & Zhu Falan · T17n0784, p. 722c) [Shinsung]: What has the most strength? Forbearance is the strongest. One who forbears bears no grudge, and is sure to be honoured among men.❞
[59] ══ DAY: AFTER THE KNIVES ══
[60] ¶ In the markets the news arrives the way all bad news arrives — ahead of the official word, behind the smell of smoke. Grain sellers count on their fingers. Children stop racing. Someone says **banquet** and means **blood**.
[61] Vendor: The king… they say he’s dead. / The commanders too. More than a hundred.
[62] Wall sentry: Some say the Eternal General saved us. / The court was sharpening first. We were next. Commoners… we say that name before we say Yeon.
[63] Gate Guard: Those blades… they say he strapped five of them to his back. / The commanders’ swords. On his own spine.
[64] Junior Guard: By Haemosu’s light… incredible… / No — terrifying. Incredible, and terrifying.
[65] Quiet man: Still… is butchering a banquet the same as saving a country.
[66] Wall sentry: Don’t say that on the wall.
[67] ¶ On the barracks steps the same argument runs until the drum tells them to stop arguing and start marching.
[68] ¶ The capital learns a new etiquette. Officials swear loyalty to the **Supreme Commander**’s door, not the nephew-king’s smile. Envoys who ask for an audience are told the kingdom is closed for inventory: of grain, of blades, of who belongs inside the walls.
[69] ── SCENE: The Yeon House ──
[70] ¶ At night the house is quieter than the city. **Yeon’s wife** has kept three boys from the sound of cheering that is not quite cheer. She waits until the lamps are few enough that even a Supreme Commander looks like a husband.
[71] Yeon's Wife: What will Tang say… / Silla too. Baekje. / Massacre. Traitor. / How those outside will name our people… even thinking of it—
[72] Yeon Gesomun: Listen… it doesn’t matter what they’ll say about us. / Do you hear me? It doesn’t matter at all — zero. Not even one bit.
[73] Yeon Gesomun: Did their ancestors die for this dirt? / Will they be standing here when it is our turn to bleed?
[74] Yeon Gesomun: So whatever they say out there about our people, our way of living — / not one second of your life. Please. / Look at me. Promise me.
[75] Yeon's Wife: …I promise. / Only — when the boys are grown, tell them that too.
[76] ¶ He nods. Outside, the drums keep time for a kingdom learning to live with its doors shut.
[77] ¶ **A kingdom with its doors shut, and a man with five swords on his back. Naturally, Chunchu wants to go and knock…!**
